official.deadline_central_display: 2 November 2026 (CSS Profile and FAFSA, Early Decision)
official.deadline_note: Regular Decision applicants file the CSS Profile and FAFSA by 1 February 2027. Brown requires applicants to indicate that they are applying for financial aid at the time they apply for admission.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle for autumn entry; aid documents are filed with the admission application
official.status_note: Brown states that international students are eligible to apply for University financial aid and that it meets full demonstrated need for admitted students who apply for financial aid at the time they apply for admission.
official.tuition_coverage_note: In most cases financial aid awards are applied directly to the student account as a credit towards the cost of tuition, fees, room and meals. Brown's published 2025-2026 charges list tuition of $71,700, fees of $2,950, housing of $10,410 and food of $8,104 against a total cost of $97,284.
benefits: Full demonstrated need met for admitted students who apply for financial aid at the time they apply for admission
The Brown Promise: all packaged loans have been replaced with scholarships in all undergraduate aid packages
Aid applied directly to the student account as a credit towards tuition, fees, room and meals
Need-blind admission for all first-year applicants, extended to international students from the Class of 2029
eligibility: International student applying for admission to Brown
Must apply for financial aid at the time of applying for admission
Financial aid is need based and Brown offers no merit awards
Brown continues to consider transfer students' financial need when making admission decisions
requirements: Indicate on the admission application that you are applying for financial aid
Submit the CSS Profile by the applicable deadline
Submit the FAFSA by the applicable deadline if a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Provide income tax forms or other materials if prompted after submitting the CSS Profile
documents: Common Application and Brown Member section
FAFSA for U.S. citizens and permanent residents
Income tax forms or other materials requested after the CSS Profile
English proficiency test results where applicable
selection_criteria: Aid is awarded entirely on demonstrated financial need
All first-year applicants are admitted on a need-blind basis
No academic merit awards exist at Brown
coverage: Travel, books and personal expenses, as stated by Brown
Not covered: vacation and summer expenses
application_method: Indicate on the admission application that you are applying for financial aid
Submit the FAFSA if a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Upload any additional materials requested after the CSS Profile
official.application_route: Apply to Brown through the Common Application, indicate that aid is sought, then file the CSS Profile and FAFSA by the round's deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international students; there is no separate application for international applicants.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible to apply for University financial aid; about 14 percent of Brown's students come from abroad.
official.description: Brown meets the full demonstrated need of admitted students who apply for financial aid at the time they apply for admission, and replaces all packaged loans with scholarships through The Brown Promise.
official.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid for international applicants
official.english_requirement: English language proficiency must be achieved before international students are admitted. Brown highly recommends that applicants for whom English is not a first language, a primary language spoken at home, or the primary language of instruction for their secondary school career submit an English proficiency test. Expected minimums published by Brown: TOEFL internet-based taken prior to January 2026, 105; TOEFL internet-based taken January 2026 and later, 5.5; IELTS 8.0; Duolingo Test of English 130; Pearson Test of English 75; C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency Cambridge English 191. Official score reports are required for matriculating students and MyBest scores are not accepted.

applicant_utility.summary: The decisive step at Brown is ticking the financial aid box on the admission application itself: Brown meets full demonstrated need only for students who apply for aid at the time they apply for admission, so an aid request added later falls outside that commitment. File the CSS Profile by 2 November 2026 for Early Decision or 1 February 2027 for Regular Decision, and expect a follow-up request for tax documents after the Profile is processed, which is the stage where most international files stall. Budget against Brown's published total cost of $97,284, and note that the award helps with travel, books and personal expenses but explicitly does not assist with vacation and summer expenses.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants who can evidence genuine financial need and who are prepared to file aid paperwork in the same round as their admission application.
application_readiness_checklist: Mark yourself as an aid applicant on the admission application before submitting it, not afterwards
Open the CSS Profile early and check which follow-up documents Brown requests, since tax uploads are requested through the Profile process
Prepare translated, complete family tax documents so a prompt can be answered within days
If you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, file the FAFSA as well, on the same deadline as the CSS Profile
Book any English test early and arrange for official score reports to reach Brown before they expire
common_rejection_risks: Applying for admission without indicating that aid is sought, which places the applicant outside the full-need commitment
Missing the separate aid deadline even though the admission application was on time
Leaving the CSS Profile follow-up document request unanswered, which holds up the award
Assuming a merit or academic scholarship exists, when Brown states it offers no merit awards
Planning a summer or vacation budget on the assumption the award covers it, which it does not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Vacation and summer expenses are explicitly not assisted. Anything outside tuition, fees, room, meals and the partial help with travel, books and personal expenses must come from family resources, savings or outside funding.
document_audit: Official English test score reports are required for matriculating students who self-report a result, and MyBest scores are not accepted
If a result will expire before May 2027, the testing agency must send the official report before expiry and a retake is required otherwise
Only the FAFSA is required for U.S. citizens and permanent residents, so international applicants should not assume it applies to them
Documents requested after the CSS Profile must arrive promptly; incomplete aid files delay the award information issued with the admission decision
alerts: Need-blind admission for international applicants begins with the Class of 2029, so applicants to earlier cohorts are still assessed with their financial need in view
Brown warns that immigration rules and restrictions on off-campus summer employment make it imperative to know exactly where funds will come from before accepting a place
Transfer applicants' financial need is still considered in the admission decision
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Common Application with the aid flag set, then the CSS Profile (and FAFSA where relevant) by the round deadline, with award details issued alongside the admission decision once the file is complete.
